goal: Test whether reusing exact dual upper-bound proofs improves correct fixed-decision risk classification at matched optimization budgets
target_venue: AAAI main-conference full paper; aspirational, not a readiness or acceptance claim
novelty_status: Unverified candidate algorithm improvement using classical weak duality; no first-in-literature claim
comparison_scope: Five implementations of the same deterministic bounded-noise finite-action certification task; not full reproductions of distinct statistical IO methods
candidate_policy: Old unregularized inverse estimator, fixed before every certification comparison, deterministic first tie on the exact parsed cost model
deployment_placeholder: First feasible action, independent of hidden costs; never used as a historical observation
shared_preprocessing: Raw action enumeration, action-cost tables, history comparisons, and fixed candidate fit are shared and timed separately. No hidden parameter or exact oracle answer enters any method.
counted_work: All method initialization, full-row insertion, LP solves, witness verification and dual-proof recycling occur inside the method timer. LP budget and wall budget both apply; timers are cooperative.
execution: Single process, one solver thread, fresh method state per task and budget; seeded random method order within each case-budget block
primary_outcome: Correct resolved classification fraction at 8 LP calls, including failed/missing/unresolved runs as zero in the denominator; average two noise conditions within each independent family-seed instance
primary_estimand: Mean paired difference dual_reuse minus full_priority over 60 new independently generated family-seed instances, stratified equally across 3 fixed families

analysis.primary_interval: Stratified paired instance bootstrap, 10000 replicates, percentile 95%; exploratory precision estimate conditional on these fixed generator families
analysis.other_comparisons: Descriptive paired effects and raw case results; no uncorrected claims of significance
analysis.missingness: No case excluded; failed/missing primary runs score zero. Accuracy, valid certificates and unresolved labels remain separate.
analysis.outliers: Retain all valid observations; timing skew summarized by median and all per-run values
analysis.normality: No Gaussian paired-test assumption. Dependence handled by averaging noise conditions within instance, not treating runs as independent samples.
analysis.power: Fixed resource-limited estimation study, not a powered confirmatory test. With paired scores bounded in [-1,1] and n=60, a distribution-free normal-approximation worst-case 95% half-width is about 0.253; actual interval comes from the declared bootstrap. No claim that n=60 suffices for a 10 percentage-point effect.

correctness_gate: Any invalid upper/lower bound, invalid witness or wrong classification under declared model blocks a success claim. Keep the failure and repair in a new explicitly identified version.
candidate_continue_rule: At least +0.10 paired resolution difference against full_priority with primary interval lower >0, and no invalid certificates; this is only an investment signal, not a novelty or generalization proof.
negative_rule: If candidate does not outperform full_priority under this rule, retain all results and do not call it a validated contribution or deploy it as a superior default.
holdout_policy: Evaluation seeds not used to choose method, thresholds or budgets; no changes after viewing evaluation results. These generator-family results are not external benchmark validation.
misspecification_policy: Report declared-set validity separately from hidden-truth regret. Truth outside the set invalidates the real-world guarantee assumptions, not necessarily the conditional certificate arithmetic.
exclusions: No LLM calls, no human subjects, no real-world language-understanding claim, no general MILP scalability claim, no probability-coverage claim
freeze_policy: Store protocol, source files, hashes, runtime versions and generated run order before method results; preserve every failed/partial run
